aiReview.summary: The PR deletes the `chatgpt-4o-latest` cards from the OpenAI and Higress model lists (aiModels and modelProviders) and updates one selector test. It never adds the recommended replacement, `gpt-5.1-chat-latest`. It also does nothing for users or agents that already have `chatgpt-4o-latest` saved; those requests will start failing after 2026-02-17. The model ID may still appear elsewhere in the repo. Typecheck, build and test all fail both before and after, so the checks prove nothing. The needs-review grade is correct.

handCheck.notes: The most substantial PR: replaces the DALL-E 2 and 3 cards with a gpt-image-2 card, switches the text-to-image service from dall-e-3 to gpt-image-2 (maps quality hd to high and the 1792 sizes to 1536, drops style, which gpt-image does not take), and makes the OpenAI-compatible textToImage accept b64_json responses as data: URLs, since gpt-image models return base64 rather than a URL. OpenAI's deprecations page confirms dall-e-2 and dall-e-3 shut down 2026-05-12 with gpt-image-2, gpt-image-1 or gpt-image-1-mini as replacements. The direction is right, but it changes behaviour the checks cannot see: images now arrive as data: URLs where the app stored remote URLs, and the DALL-E tool's style option silently stops doing anything. The payload type also offers gpt-image-1-mini, which this run's own watcher lists as retiring 2026-12-01. I would merge after checking how generated images are stored and shown, and after dropping the retiring model from the type. Checked by reading the diff, the PR body and OpenAI's deprecations page; nothing was run.

aiReview.summary: The diff removes the only `payment_method_types` usage, the `checkout.sessions.create` call at src/trpc/controller/index.ts:102. The other named call sites (the `subscriptions.retrieve` calls and `billingPortal.sessions.create`) don't use this parameter and correctly need no change. The problem is that a plain deletion changes behaviour. The session now falls back to dynamic payment methods, so customers see whatever is enabled in the Stripe Dashboard instead of exactly card and PayPal. That may drop PayPal, which must be enabled and eligible for recurring payments, or add methods that weren't offered before. Passing `allowed_payment_method_types: ['card', 'paypal']` would keep today's behaviour. The checks prove nothing: typecheck (6 errors) and build (1 failure) fail the same way before and after, and no checkout session is created against Stripe. The needs-review grade fits.

handCheck.notes: Deletes payment_method_types: ['card', 'paypal'] from checkout.sessions.create (src/trpc/controller/index.ts:105). Stripe's Endive page confirms the removal (a 400 on 2026-09-30.endive) and names allowed_payment_method_types as the way to keep a fixed set. But the repo is on stripe-node 14.13.0 with no apiVersion, so it sends 2023-10-16, where the param still works: deleting it now switches checkout to dynamic payment methods (PayPal may disappear, others may appear) before anything forces it. The PR body says this. needs-review is right: typecheck and build fail before and after on pre-existing errors. Superseded by the node-v23-0-0 PR, which renames the param together with the SDK upgrade. Checked by reading the diff, the PR body, the files at the pinned commit and Stripe's changelog page; nothing was run.

No breaking Endive items are adopted, so the listed call sites in route.ts and trpc/controller/index.ts need no code change. needs-review is the right grade: typecheck (6) and build (1) fail identically before and after, so the checks prove nothing either way. The webhook path is untouched. Its payload shape is set by the endpoint's api_version in the Stripe dashboard, which this diff cannot control.

handCheck.notes: The real migration. Bumps stripe ^14.13.0 to ^23.0.0 (package.json and package-lock.json), moves both current_period_end reads in src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts (lines 47 and 66) to subscription.items.data[0].current_period_end, and renames payment_method_types to allowed_payment_method_types in checkout.sessions.create, the replacement Stripe's Endive page names. The other Stripe calls (subscriptions.retrieve reading cancel_at_period_end in src/lib/stripe.ts, billingPortal.sessions.create, webhooks.constructEvent with the raw body and default tolerance) need no change I can see. Typecheck and build fail before and after on pre-existing errors: implicit any, and no Prisma client because postinstall (prisma generate) does not run with install scripts off. So nothing is proven, and needs-review is right. I would merge it after a test-mode checkout and webhook replay on Node 20 or later (v23 drops Node 18; the node-v23-drop-node18 task that would have checked this was unrun). The AI reviewer's three high concerns are wrong: allowed_payment_method_types is a real Endive param, src/lib/stripe.ts reads cancel_at_period_end rather than current_period_end, and the client pins no apiVersion. It saw only the diff, not those files. Checked by reading the diff, the PR body, the files at the pinned commit and Stripe's changelog page; nothing was run.

Merge blocker: engines is 26.x while serverless.yml moves Lambda to nodejs24.x, because AWS offers no nodejs26.x (the PR says so). The health handler ships on 24 in a package that declares 26, so engines should be 24.x until Lambda has 26 or the Lambda code should be split out. The PR body contradicts itself: 'pass on the old runtime' and 'before on the sandbox default'. Its table proves one test run, on 26 only after. I built the Dockerfile from the PR: node v26.13.0, src/app.js loads, so the 'image was not built' caveat is now checked by hand. The floating node:26 tag is a choice for a person. Needs-review is the right grade.

The code is a reasonable marking and the unproven section is honest. Two things to fix before merging. The test hard-codes ai_model: 'text-davinci-003' instead of using MODEL: I merged this PR with demo-node-api#3 and ran npm test in Docker on node 22, and it fails 1 of 5, so whichever lands second breaks. The title is the raw obligation sentence cut off mid-word. Whether the operator is a 'provider' and whether a header meets the robustness duty is for a person or lawyer; the PR says so and never claims compliance. Needs-review is right.

The migration to chat.completions is correct and gpt-5.6-luna is on OpenAI's models page. Blockers: the title names gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, which the PR itself says is shut down and did not use. max_completion_tokens stays at 200 on a reasoning model, so a summary can come back empty, and message.content may be null, which would throw at .trim() and return 502. The PR flags the budget risk but left it. Not run against a live API; test only uses a mock. It collides with demo-node-api#2's test. Needs-review is right.

A correct two-line bump: Flask and Werkzeug have to move together. The PR's own check failed before and after because the sandbox used Python 3.12 while the repo requires >=3.9,<3.10, so stripe 2.76.0 could not import. I ran the 7 repo tests in Docker on python:3.9 with flask 3.1.3, werkzeug 3.1.9 and the real stripe 2.76.0: 7 passed. That is by hand; the PR doesn't prove it, so needs-review stays right. The harness should pick the Python the repo declares (for lane O4). The 'deadline 2023-09-30' in the body is a release date (lane F4). Best candidate for the merge test.
